newsitem.title: USA: Blue-chip stocks cautious ahead of Fed decision.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chip stocks cautious ahead of Fed decision.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks gave back most of their strong gains at midsession Wednesday as investors awaited the conclusion of the two-day meeting of Federal Reserve policy-makers to set the course for interest rates.
At 1 p.m. EST, the Dow Jones industrial average was up 13.09 points at 6,846.57 after gaining more than 40 points initially.
In the broader market, advances led declines by a small margin on active volume of 301 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq composite index was down 9.39 to 1,364.36, and the American Stock Exchange index was off 1.17 at 588.08.
The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee, which has been meeting since Tuesday, is expected to announce its decision at about 2:15 p.m. (1915 GMT)
The Fed has held rates steady for more than a year, since cutting them by a quarter percentage point on Jan. 31, 1996, and Wall Street is betting that it will again keep interest rates unchanged.

"I think people are waiting to make sure there are no surprises out of the Fed," said Frank Calta, director of trading at Anvil Institutional Services. "If that's the case, maybe things will heat up again."
Analysts said stocks got some support from President Clinton's State of the Union pledge to seek a balanced budget.

Clinton "appears to be anxious to see the enactment of a balanced budget and that's good for the bond market and the economy as a whole," said Alan Ackerman, senior vice president at Fahnestock and Co.

The bond market slipped after giving up an early gains. The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond was off 6/32, which raised its yield to 6.72 percent from 6.71 percent on Tuesday. Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions.
Analysts said the renewed weakness in technology stocks weighed on the market, as downgrades by brokerage houses of heavyweight Intel Corp. soured investor' sentiment.
"The tech stocks seem to be out of steam here," said Calta.

A proposed stock-swap merger between Morgan Stanley Group Inc. and Dean Witter Discover & Co. focused investor attention on brokerage house stocks. The two said they were creating a financial giant with a combined market capitalisation of $21 billion.
"I suspect there will probably be some additional consolidation" in the brokerage industry, said Michael LaTronica, director of research at Gruntal & Co.

Morgan Stanley shot up 7-5/8 to 65 and Dean Witter added 1-5/8 to 40-1/4. Elsewhere in the group, Merrill Lynch & Co. rose 1-5/8 to 87, Salomon Inc. added 1 to 56-1/2 and A.G. Edwards Inc. gained 2 to 36-1/2.

Bucking the trend was PaineWebber Group Inc., which was off 3-1/2 to 35-3/8. The stock had surged in recent sessions on market rumours that it would be the target of a takeover, possibly by Morgan Stanley.
Intel dropped 4-5/8 to 160-1/8 after Prudential Securities and Gruntal downgraded the stock, both citing the stock's price as the reason.
The downturn in Intel hit other high tech shares, including International Business Machines Corp., which dropped 3-5/8 to 150-1/4. Microsoft Corp. shed 2 to 101-1/8.
Among other technology shares, computer networking company Cisco Systems Inc. shed 2-3/8 to 64-3/4.
Analysts linked the weakness to cautious comments by Cisco officials about the company's traditionally weak April quarter.
